c.tagline: A Belle Époque beach resort on the Basque coast, and the birthplace of European surfing

card: Widely accepted; cash useful for small shops and beach vendors

taxi.fare: Metered, roughly €4 flag fall plus per-km rate
taxi.fareNote: Metered fares are standard and reliable

emergency.note: 112 is the general EU-style emergency number that connects to police, fire, and ambulance

walk: Central Biarritz and its beaches are compact and walkable; surf spots along the Cote des Basques are a scenic coastal walk or short bus ride

safety.safety: Very safe resort town, popular with families and surfers alike
safety.crime: Petty theft on crowded beaches is the main concern

hood_landmark.Grande Plage: The Grande Plage and Hotel du Palais
hood_landmark.Cote des Basques: The Cote des Basques surf beach
hood_landmark.Port Vieux: The sheltered Port Vieux swimming cove
hood_landmark.Rocher de la Vierge: The Rocher de la Vierge statue and footbridge

avoid.reason: Watch belongings on Grande Plage and around the beachfront in summer, when opportunistic thefts of unattended bags occur.

hood_desc: The grand main beach lined with the historic Hotel du Palais and casino, the postcard image of Biarritz.
The birthplace of European surfing, with consistent beach breaks and surf schools lining the promenade.
A small, sheltered cove popular with families for calmer swimming than the open Atlantic beaches.
The lively market and shopping district just inland from the beaches, with the best everyday dining options.
A rocky outcrop connected by footbridge, offering dramatic ocean views and a lighthouse-lined coastal walk.

water.note: Tap water is safe to drink throughout France.

transit.sys: Chronoplus urban bus network (also serves Bayonne and Anglet)
transit.pay: Cash or contactless card on board; rechargeable travel card available
transit.note: Central Biarritz is very walkable; buses connect to Bayonne, Anglet, and the airport

transport.air: Biarritz Pays Basque Airport (BIQ), about 10 min from downtown
transport.train: TGV and regional trains connect via Biarritz-La Negresse station to Bordeaux and Paris
transport.bus: Regional buses connect to San Sebastian, Spain and other Basque coast towns
transport.car: Well connected via the A63 motorway; parking near the beaches fills quickly in summer

net.w: Free wifi standard in hotels and cafes
net.ap: An Orange, SFR, or Bouygues tourist SIM or eSIM

tip.s: Not obligatory; rounding up is appreciated for surf instructors and guides
tip.r: Service is included by law; rounding up is a nice gesture, not expected
